title: Disney Eyes Thousands of Layoffs, Managers Asked to Cut 20% (DIS)
summary: Gotrade News - Walt Disney (DIS) is weighing thousands of job cuts and has asked some managers to find 20% in annual cost savings, Reuters reported,
body_markdown:
In the same release, Disney said it continues to expect fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS growth of approximately 12% excluding the impact of the 53rd week, and approximately 16% including it. The company also said it is now targeting at least $9 billion in share repurchases in fiscal 2026.


## Disney Layoff Rounds: 7,000 Roles in 2023, About 1,000 in April


Reuters and BlogMickey list the earlier rounds of cuts below.


Period Reported cuts Source


2023 About 7,000 roles, part of a $5.5 billion savings effort under former CEO Bob Iger Reuters


2025 Several hundred jobs Reuters


April 2026 About 1,000 positions Reuters


September 2026 A few hundred employees in human resources and technology Reuters


October 27, 2026 159 permanent layoffs at Walt Disney Imagineering's Glendale site, effective December 29, per a California WARN notice BlogMickey


October 28, 2026 100 to 200 Disney Experiences employees, mostly at Imagineering BlogMickey


Disney is not alone.[Netflix (NFLX)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/nflx/) and Skydance, which acquired Warner Bros Discovery earlier this year, have also cut jobs, Reuters reported. BlogMickey tied the industry cuts to falling traditional TV revenue and slowing streaming growth, and quoted Disney President Dana Walden at Bloomberg's Screentime conference in Los Angeles:


> "There is a need to constantly evaluate how you're structured and how big is the organization."


## What It Means for DIS Ahead of November 17 Earnings


Disney reports full fiscal 2026 results on November 17, and BlogMickey called that[earnings report](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/how-to-read-an-earnings-report/) the next scheduled chance for D'Amaro to address the cuts publicly. Until then, neither the job count nor the divisions affected have been confirmed.


Disney Experiences, the parks and cruise unit whose inclusion in the target is unclear, brought in $36.2 billion of fiscal 2025 revenue and more than 56% of operating income, and about 80% of Disney's employees work there, according to BlogMickey.
